'''''Chrysanthemum indicum''''' is a flowering plant commonly called '''Indian chrysanthemum''',<ref name=grin>{{GRIN |accessdate=30 July 2014}}</ref> within the family [[Asteraceae]] and genus ''[[Chrysanthemum]]''.

==Description==
''Chrysanthemum indicum'' grows up to {{convert|1|m|ft|0|abbr=on}}<ref name=":1" /> tall and {{convert|0.6|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} across. It usually blooms from August to October, producing yellow or white flowers and yellow pollen.

== Distribution and habitat ==
It grows outside under sunlight with moist soil. It can tolerate light (sandy), medium (loamy) and heavy (clay) soils. The soil can be [[Soil pH|acidic]], neutral, or [[Alkali soil|alkaline]].<ref>https://www.pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Chrysanthemum+indicum (Moul., n.d.)</ref>

==Cultivation==
[[File:Flowers of Chrysanthemum indicum, photographed in West Bengal, on January 9, 2023.jpg|thumb|Full bloom flowers of Chrysanthemum indicum in [[West Bengal]], India.]]
''Chrysanthemum indicum'' is a plant of the [[temperate zone]] but it can be grown successfully outside the area such as in tropical areas as it is often cultivated in Southeast Asia with moist soil (pH around 6.5) in sunny weather. It can handle temperatures down to {{convert|-10|C|F}}. Seeds can be sowed between the range of August to October. It usually starts to grow in 10 to 18 days at {{convert|15|C|F}}.

==Uses==
The flower heads are pickled in vinegar.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Wholesale Chrysanthemum Indicum Flowers |url=https://www.josephflach.co.uk/wholesale/chrysanthemum-indicum-flowers/ |access-date=2024-07-25 |website=Joseph Flach & Sons |language=en-GB}}</ref> The flowers can be used to make drinks such as [[chrysanthemum tea]], and the young leaves can also be steeped or cooked.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Chrysanthemum indicum |url=https://tropical.theferns.info/viewtropical.php?id=Chrysanthemum+indicum |access-date=2024-07-25 |website=Useful Tropical Plants}}</ref> The petals can also be [[Blanching (cooking)|blanched]] for use in salads and other dishes.<ref name=":0" />
